title: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation and Amortized Write Dynamics in PHP-Based B-Tree and LSM-Tree Engines
topic: Storage Engines Explained: B-Tree vs LSM Tree
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: This paper investigates the algorithmic invariants and empirical performance of two canonical storage engines---B-Tree and Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tre...
abstract: This paper investigates the algorithmic invariants and empirical performance of two canonical storage engines---B-Tree and Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree)---implemented in PHP. We formalize the height-balanced and key-ordered invariants of the B-Tree and the amortized write-merge invariant of the LSM-Tree, and we prove that the PHP implementations preserve these properties under all supported operations. An experimental campaign on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, and Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure, yields a mean latency of 38 736.57 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 40 040.39 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 25 815 ops/s. These results confirm that PHP can serve as a viable platform for lightweight storage engines while maintaining rigorous algorithmic guarantees. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261118_050251_storage_engines_explained__b-t}
